The invention relates to a mold for a device for manufacturing particle foam articles. The mold delimits a mold cavity. The mold includes a mold chase and at least one mold plate movable relative to the mold chase. The mold chase is characterized in that it comprises front walls that are formed to be more rigid than the inner wall facing the mold cavity. According to another aspect of the invention, the mold plate comprises a reinforcing structure, which is formed independently of a hollow chamber structure of the mold plate, wherein vapor is conducted exclusively through the hollow chamber structure of the mold plate. Furthermore, fins of the hollow chamber structure can be arranged slanted, so that condensed water forming in the hollow chamber structure flows away from the inner wall of the mold plate. According to another aspect, a sealing element is provided, which surrounds the mold plate. The sealing element is formed as an inflatable tube.

The invention concerns a mold for equipment used to produce particle-foam articles. This mold defines a molding cavity and has a mold chase together with at least one mold plate that can move relative to the mold chase. The mold chase is distinguished by front walls that have greater rigidity than the inner wall directed toward the molding cavity.

outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a mold for manufacturing particle foam articles, wherein the mold defines a mold cavity in which the particle foam article is formed. The mold is designed to withstand the mechanical loads occurring during the molding process while also enabling efficient supply and removal of process media, such as vapor and condensate.

The mold comprises a mold chase and at least one mold plate that is movable relative to the mold chase. By moving the mold plate, the size or configuration of the mold cavity can be adjusted, or the mold can be opened and closed for filling, molding, and demolding operations. The mold chase provides a supporting frame or outer mold structure, while the movable mold plate forms at least part of the boundary of the mold cavity.

The mold chase includes front walls and an inner wall facing the mold cavity. The front walls are designed to be more rigid than the inner wall. This difference in rigidity allows the mold chase to provide high structural stability where major forces are introduced or supported, while the inner wall may be optimized for thermal behavior, weight reduction, or interaction with the molding process. In particular, the more rigid front walls can absorb and distribute mechanical stresses, thereby improving dimensional accuracy and durability of the mold during repeated production cycles.

The mold plate comprises a hollow chamber structure through which vapor is conducted during operation. In addition, the mold plate includes a reinforcing structure that is independent of the hollow chamber structure. As a result, the functions of mechanical reinforcement and vapor guidance are separated from one another. The reinforcing structure increases the stiffness and strength of the mold plate without interfering with the flow of vapor. Vapor is conducted exclusively through the hollow chamber structure, which can therefore be specifically configured for uniform vapor distribution and efficient heating of the mold cavity.

Within the hollow chamber structure, slanted fins are provided. These fins guide or support vapor flow and, in particular, assist in removing condensed water from the region of the mold plate’s inner wall. Because the fins are inclined, condensate can flow away from the inner wall under the influence of gravity or pressure differences, reducing the risk of water accumulation near the molding surface. This improves thermal efficiency, promotes more uniform heating, and can contribute to better surface quality of the particle foam article.

The mold plate is further surrounded by an inflatable tube sealing element. This sealing element can be inflated to form a tight seal between the mold plate and adjacent mold components, such as the mold chase. The inflatable seal accommodates relative movement of the mold plate and compensates for tolerances while helping to prevent leakage of vapor, air, or condensate during the molding process. Overall, the mold combines high mechanical stability, efficient vapor management, improved condensate drainage, and reliable sealing, thereby supporting the manufacture of high-quality particle foam articles in an efficient and reproducible manner.
outputs.L4:
The invention relates to a mold for manufacturing particle foam articles, in particular articles made from expanded thermoplastic foam particles such as expanded polypropylene, expanded polyethylene, expandable polystyrene, or similar bead-foam materials. The mold is designed to improve mechanical stability, vapor distribution, condensate removal, and sealing during the molding process, while allowing accurate formation of the foam article in the mold cavity.

The mold comprises a mold chase that at least partially surrounds a mold cavity in which the particle foam article is produced. The mold chase includes a cavity-facing inner wall and front walls arranged at the outer side or end regions of the mold chase. According to the invention, the front walls of the mold chase are formed so as to be more rigid than the inner wall facing the mold cavity. This configuration provides the mold chase with high overall dimensional stability and resistance to deformation during molding, especially when the mold is exposed to internal vapor pressure, mechanical closing forces, and thermal cycling. At the same time, the cavity-facing inner wall can be configured with a lower rigidity, which may reduce stress concentrations, facilitate heat transfer, or allow the wall to be adapted more effectively to the geometry of the foam article.

The mold further comprises a movable mold plate that can be displaced relative to the mold chase. This mold plate forms at least part of the boundary of the mold cavity and may be moved for opening and closing the mold, for compressing the foam particles, or for demolding the finished article. The movable mold plate is provided with an independent reinforcing structure. This reinforcing structure is separate from the vapor-conducting structure of the mold plate and is arranged to absorb mechanical loads acting on the mold plate during operation. By decoupling the reinforcing function from the vapor-guiding function, the mold plate can be made both mechanically stable and efficient in terms of vapor distribution.

The movable mold plate also includes hollow chambers through which process vapor can be conducted. During manufacture of a particle foam article, vapor is introduced into the mold in order to heat and fuse the foam particles. The hollow chambers in the mold plate serve as vapor channels or vapor distribution spaces, enabling the vapor to be guided in a controlled manner to selected regions of the mold cavity. The vapor can pass through openings, nozzles, slots, or permeable regions into the cavity so that the foam particles are uniformly heated and welded together. This improves the quality of the finished foam article and reduces the risk of insufficient fusion, uneven density, or surface defects.

In a preferred embodiment, fins are arranged in the hollow chambers of the movable mold plate. These fins may reinforce the structure of the hollow chambers and may also influence the flow of vapor and condensate. The fins are advantageously arranged at an inclination or slant rather than extending horizontally. By providing slanted fins, condensate that forms when the vapor cools inside the mold plate can drain away more reliably. This prevents the accumulation of water in the hollow chambers and reduces the risk that condensate will be carried into the mold cavity in an uncontrolled manner. Improved water removal contributes to a more stable molding process, shorter cycle times, and improved surface quality of the particle foam article.

The mold may further include a seal arranged around the movable mold plate. In particular, an inflatable tube seal can be positioned between the movable mold plate and an adjacent mold component, such as the mold chase. When the mold is closed, the tube seal can be inflated so that it presses against the surrounding sealing surfaces and forms a tight seal around the mold plate. This prevents vapor, air, or condensate from escaping from the mold cavity or from the vapor-conducting regions. After completion of the molding process, the seal can be deflated to reduce friction and allow the movable mold plate to be displaced more easily. The inflatable tube seal therefore provides reliable sealing during processing while permitting smooth movement of the mold plate during opening and closing.

The combination of the rigid front walls of the mold chase, the less rigid cavity-facing inner wall, the independently reinforced movable mold plate, the vapor-conducting hollow chambers, the slanted condensate-draining fins, and the inflatable tube seal results in a mold that is particularly suitable for producing high-quality particle foam articles. The mold maintains its shape under pressure and thermal load, distributes vapor efficiently, removes condensate in a controlled manner, and seals effectively during operation. These features help improve process reliability, reduce defects, shorten molding cycles, and extend the service life of the mold.

The mold further includes vapor chambers arranged to supply heating vapor to the mold cavity through the movable mold plate and/or associated mold inserts. counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a brief “field and summary of the invention” section for a patent application describing improvements to molds for manufacturing particle foam parts, focusing on rigidity differences in the mold chase, a separately reinforced mold plate, controlled vapor flow through hollow chamber structures, angled fins, and an inflatable tube seal.
counterfactuals.output:
## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates generally to molds for manufacturing particle foam parts, including expandable or expanded polymer bead foam components. More particularly, the invention relates to mold assemblies having improved structural rigidity, vapor distribution, sealing, and thermal control features for use in forming particle foam articles.

## Summary of the Invention

In one aspect, the invention provides an improved mold assembly for manufacturing particle foam parts. The mold assembly includes a mold chase having regions of differing rigidity, such that selected portions of the chase provide enhanced structural support while other portions may be configured to reduce weight, improve manufacturability, or accommodate thermal expansion. The rigidity differences may be achieved through variations in material thickness, geometry, reinforcement placement, ribbing, or combinations thereof.

In another aspect, the mold assembly includes a mold plate that is separately reinforced from the mold chase. The reinforced mold plate may provide increased resistance to deflection during molding operations, including during steam or vapor injection, pressurization, cooling, and demolding. By reinforcing the mold plate separately, the mold cavity geometry may be maintained with greater precision while permitting the chase to be optimized for other structural or thermal requirements.

In a further aspect, the mold assembly includes one or more hollow chamber structures configured to control vapor flow through the mold. The hollow chamber structures may define internal passages, plenums, or distribution volumes that direct steam, vapor, air, or other process fluids to selected regions of the mold cavity. The chambers may improve uniformity of heating and fusion of the particle foam material while reducing cycle time and energy consumption.

In some embodiments, the hollow chamber structures include angled fins positioned to influence vapor flow, heat transfer, condensate drainage, or mechanical stiffness. The angled fins may direct vapor toward predetermined regions, promote turbulence or distribution within a chamber, increase surface area for heat transfer, and/or provide reinforcement to the chamber structure.

In yet another aspect, the mold assembly includes an inflatable tube seal positioned between cooperating mold components. The inflatable tube seal may be selectively pressurized to form a seal during molding operations and depressurized to facilitate mold opening, part removal, cleaning, or maintenance. The seal may accommodate dimensional variation, thermal expansion, and repeated mold cycling while reducing leakage of vapor or process fluid.

Together, these features provide a mold assembly having improved rigidity control, enhanced cavity stability, controlled vapor distribution, improved sealing, and more efficient manufacture of particle foam parts.

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate a concise technical summary of an invention for a particle foam article manufacturing mold that emphasizes the mold chase structure, movable mold plate, independent reinforcing structure, hollow chamber vapor conduction, angled condensate-draining fins, and inflatable sealing element.
counterfactuals.output:
A particle foam article manufacturing mold comprises a mold chase structure supporting a movable mold plate that defines, at least in part, a molding cavity for forming a particle foam component. The movable mold plate is mechanically supported by an independent reinforcing structure separate from the vapor-conducting portions of the mold, enabling high dimensional stability and reduced deformation under molding pressure and thermal cycling.

The mold plate includes or is coupled to hollow chamber structures configured to conduct vapor, steam, or other process media for heating and processing the particle foam material. Within the hollow chamber, angled fins are arranged to reinforce the plate while guiding condensate toward drainage regions, improving condensate removal and thermal efficiency. The fins are inclined relative to the mold plate surface to promote gravity-assisted flow and reduce liquid accumulation in the vapor chamber.

An inflatable sealing element is positioned between cooperating mold components, such as between the mold chase and movable mold plate or adjacent mold sections. The sealing element is selectively pressurizable to establish a process-tight seal during molding and depressurizable to facilitate opening, movement, or demolding. The combination of an independently reinforced movable mold plate, integrated vapor-conducting hollow chambers, condensate-draining angled fins, and inflatable sealing provides a robust, thermally efficient mold system for producing particle foam articles with improved process reliability and mold longevity.
